intro.line: Theros. A world of sea and sun and bronze, where the gods walk in the night sky of Nyx and listen to every prayer.
Here, the gods exist because mortals believe in them. Faith makes them, and faith feeds them.
Elspeth Tirel came here to rest after Mirrodin fell. She did not get to rest for long.
I was not chosen for my faith in the gods. Sometimes the gods must put their faith in us.

finale.line: In Nyx, among the stars, Elspeth drives the Godsend through the god of revels.
Heliod watches the mortal who has just killed a god. He gave her the spear. He takes it back.
Elspeth Tirel dies on Theros, at the hand of the god she served. Ajani carries the news down from Nyx.
All peoples treasure a place where the weary traveler may drink in peace.
She found one here. That is what I will remember.

villainFinale.line: Xenagos sits in Nyx with the other gods, and the revel never ends.
The gods of Theros are born of the expectations and beliefs of mortals. If I have found godhood, what does that say about their true desires?
Embrace every moment, for it could be your last.

battles.title: Deathbellow Canyon
battles.blurb: You arrive on a hot white road outside Akros. Minotaur raiders have come up out of Deathbellow Canyon, and Elspeth Tirel is holding the pass with the Akroan hoplites.

scene.line: It has been my experience that soldiers most fervently follow generals who lead by example.
"You. Poet. Be sure to write this down."
Heroic: whenever you cast a spell that targets a heroic creature, it triggers. Bless your heroes, and they grow.

villainScene.line: Their only dreams are of full stomachs.
Deathbellow Canyon is home to minotaurs and many other creatures that share a love for the taste of human flesh.
A minotaur does not distinguish between human, satyr, and triton. They are all meat.

after.line: The priests say Heliod is watching me. I came here to stop being watched.

battles.title: The Crashing Wave
battles.blurb: Out on the sea, the merfolk planeswalker Kiora has decided that a god of the sea is just a rival with good publicity. Thassa's tritons disagree.

scene.line: I will match Thassa drop for drop and show a god what true power is.
I want one.
Bestow: some creatures can be cast as an Aura instead. If the creature they enchant dies, they fall off and stay as a creature.

villainScene.line: Mortal strength, like mortal hope, is so easily crushed.
When mortals claim there are places Thassa cannot reach, the sea god laughs.

after.line: I can see why this appeals to Thassa.

battles.title: The Sun and the Dead
battles.blurb: Heliod, the sun god, and Erebos, the god of the dead, are brothers, and they have never agreed on anything. Their faithful settle it with a duel at the edge of the Underworld.

scene.line: Legend speaks of the Sun Spear, the mighty weapon that can strike any point in Theros, even the depths of the Underworld.
Devotion: count the coloured mana symbols in the costs of your permanents. The gods only walk as creatures when your devotion is high enough.

villainScene.line: A body Returned, a soul still lost.
The sailor had never seen a god before. Now she had gazed upon Thassa. Shortly she would see Athreos, and then she would meet Erebos.

after.line: Two gods and their followers bled for a family argument. Remind me why we pray to them.

battles.title: The Revel
battles.blurb: Ajani Goldmane, a leonin planeswalker and an old friend of Elspeth's, has come to Theros to find her. In the hills he finds Xenagos instead: a satyr planeswalker whose revels have started to look like worship.

scene.line: All peoples treasure a place where the weary traveler may drink in peace.
Monstrosity: pay a creature's monstrosity cost once and it gets bigger for good, often with a bonus. Kill it before they can afford it.

villainScene.line: Why pray to the gods, who feed on your worship? Dissolve your illusions and see the true nature of things.
Stoke a fire hot enough and you'll never run out of things to burn.

after.line: You think the gods are real because people believe in them? Then watch what happens when they believe in me.

battles.title: Nightmares
battles.blurb: In the woods of Setessa, children are going missing and the dreams are going wrong. Anthousa, a Setessan hero, is tracking something that is not a monster. It is a planeswalker called Ashiok, who feeds on nightmares.

scene.line: More children taken. This is an evil we will track without mercy.
The emotional echoes of dryad gatherings attract lost souls.
Constellation: whenever an enchantment enters under your control, a constellation card triggers. Play your enchantments one by one.

villainScene.line: Every nightmare is a caged bird that yearns to be set free.
Not all nightmares can be escaped by waking.
To think some believe it peaceful to die in one's sleep.

after.line: It saddens me to lose a source of inspiration. This one seemed especially promising.

battles.title: Master of Waves
battles.blurb: The Archive remembers late 2013, when Mono-Blue Devotion turned Thassa into a creature and flooded the board with Master of Waves tokens, against the Red-Green Monsters deck and its dragons.

deck.name: Mono-Blue Devotion
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from cards in this act's sets only, so Tidebinder Mage, Frostburn Weird, Cloudfin Raptor and Nightveil Specter are not in it.

scene.line: To resist Thassa is to deny the rising tide.
Every blue symbol on the table is one more Elemental from Master of Waves.

villainScene.line: Stoke a fire hot enough and you'll never run out of things to burn.

battles.title: Heroes and Burn
battles.blurb: The Archive remembers 2014: heroic decks that turned one small creature into a monster with a stack of cheap spells, against mono-red burn that never let a creature live long enough.

deck.name: Heroic
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from cards in this act's sets only, so Feat of Resistance and Hopeful Initiate are not in it.

scene.line: It's never good to walk into an ambush, but with the right spell you might walk out again.
Hold a protection spell for their burn. One protected hero wins this.

villainScene.line: Thakolides the Mighty / Slayer of minotaurs / Vanquisher of giants / Killed by a scorpion

battles.title: The God of Revels
battles.blurb: Xenagos did it. Enough mortals danced in his name that he rose into Nyx as a god. Heliod gives Elspeth his own weapon, the Godsend, and sends her and Ajani up into the stars after him.

scene.line: The false god Xenagos treats the whole world as his rollick site. If his whims are left unchecked, Theros will be reduced to rubble and ashes.
A tiny flame is enough to dispel the night.
I am with you. Whatever is up there.

villainScene.line: The gods of Theros are born of the expectations and beliefs of mortals. If I have found godhood, what does that say about their true desires?
Embrace every moment, for it could be your last.

half.line: He is only as strong as his dancers. Cut them down.

battles.title: Gray Merchant
battles.blurb: Deep in the archive, the deck that was the format for a season.

archive.format: Standard: Return to Ravnica block, Theros block and Magic 2014 or 2015.
archive.what: A black deck that took the opponent's best card with Thoughtseize, killed every threat with Hero's Downfall, and piled black mana symbols onto the table until Gray Merchant of Asphodel drained the opponent for a game's worth of life.
archive.why: It was one of the most played and most successful decks of its Standard season.
archive.beat: Go big and go early. Their removal is one-for-one, so play more threats than they have answers, and keep your life total high for the Merchants.
archive.after: This tribute uses only this act's sets, so Pack Rat, Desecration Demon, Underworld Connections and Nightveil Specter are not in it.

deck.name: Mono-Black Devotion
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from cards in this act's sets only. No single tournament list is copied.

scene.line: "It is not yours to hunt, mortal. Be content with its beauty alone."
Too many threats for their removal. That is the whole plan.

villainScene.line: Knowledge is such a burden. Release it. Release all your fears to me.
Destiny exalts a chosen few, but even heroes break.
